skill.name: google-agents-cli-workflow
skill.description: Guides coding agents through designing, scaffolding, building, evaluating, deploying, publishing, and observing Google ADK agents with agents-cli.
skill.summary: Manage the Google ADK agent lifecycle with structured design, evaluation, deployment, and troubleshooting guidance.
skill.author: google

security_audit.summary: Review found that 94 of 97 alerts are contextual false positives caused by Markdown, CLI documentation, and official documentation links. Three high-severity findings are confirmed because the workflow can place secret-bearing `.env` files in agent context or generated projects. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The workflow asks agents to adapt or preserve `.env` files that may contain credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Use `.env.example` files with placeholders. Never read, copy, display, or send secret values unless the user explicitly authorizes the exact operation.

remediation.issue: Project configuration guidance does not separate non-secret settings from secret values.
remediation.suggestion: Read only named non-secret variables. Keep credentials in GCP Secret Manager and redact secrets from prompts, logs, diffs, and generated artifacts.

content.user_title: Build and Operate Google ADK Agents
content.value_statement: Agent projects often lose consistency between design, testing, deployment, and operations. This skill guides coding agents through a structured agents-cli and Google ADK workflow.
actual_capabilities: Guides requirement discovery and records an approved agent specification.
Routes projects through agents-cli scaffolding and relevant ADK reference recipes.
Separates local smoke tests, code tests, and behavioral agent evaluations.
Guides deployment approval, target configuration, publishing, and observability phases.
Preserves unrelated code, models, configuration, comments, and formatting during changes.
Provides troubleshooting steps for CLI, state, configuration, and deployment failures.
limitations: Requires google-agents-cli and its related phase-specific skills for complete workflows.
Does not replace project-specific security review, access control, or compliance validation.
Does not guarantee agent quality; users must define thresholds and review evaluation results.
Current publishing guidance targets Gemini Enterprise and may not cover other registries.

use_cases.title: Create an ADK agent
use_cases.description: Turn an idea into an approved specification, select reference recipes, scaffold the project, and implement the first working agent.

use_cases.title: Evaluate an existing agent
use_cases.description: Build focused evaluation cases, separate deterministic tests from behavior checks, and iterate until agreed quality thresholds pass.

use_cases.title: Deploy and operate an agent
use_cases.description: Select a Google Cloud target, require deployment approval, publish when needed, and establish production observability.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a simple agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a simple ADK agent for [purpose]. Ask one question at a time, then write a short specification for approval.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold an approved design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review `.agents-cli-spec.md`, identify matching ADK recipes, and scaffold [project name]. Preserve existing files and explain each planned command before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate agent behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a focused evaluation plan for [agent]. Include core cases, measurable thresholds, tool-use checks, safety criteria, and an iteration sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare production deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [project] for deployment to [target]. Verify evaluation results, configuration, secret handling, rollback readiness, publishing needs, and observability before requesting approval.

output_examples.input: Design a support agent that searches internal product documentation.
output: Recommended architecture: one ADK agent with a retrieval tool and explicit citation requirements.
Open decision: confirm the documentation source and authentication method before scaffolding.
Next gate: approve the specification before studying the retrieval recipe.

output_examples.input: Prepare my evaluated agent for Cloud Run.
output: Deployment readiness: evaluation thresholds pass and the target is configured.
Required review: confirm secret storage, service identity, rollback plan, and logging settings.
Approval gate: deployment will not run until explicit human approval.

best_practices: Approve the specification before scaffolding or modifying project code.
Use agents-cli evaluation for behavioral quality and pytest for deterministic code correctness.
Require explicit human approval before deployment and keep secrets outside model context.
anti_patterns: Do not skip reference recipes for retrieval, memory, approvals, authentication, or sandboxed execution.
Do not replace a scaffolded model or unrelated configuration without an explicit user request.
Do not treat one successful local prompt as sufficient behavioral validation.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It guides development of Google ADK agents from initial design through evaluation, deployment, publishing, and production observation.

faq.question: Does it create a project without approval?
faq.answer: No. It requires an approved specification before scaffolding and explicit human approval before deployment.

faq.question: Which tools are required?
faq.answer: The workflow requires google-agents-cli. It also expects uv and phase-specific companion skills for scaffolding, coding, evaluation, deployment, publishing, and observability.

faq.question: How are agent behaviors tested?
faq.answer: Use agents-cli evaluation for response quality, tool use, persona, and safety. Use pytest only for deterministic code behavior.

faq.question: Can it modify an existing project?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide project enhancement while preserving unrelated code, configuration, comments, models, and formatting.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Store secrets in GCP Secret Manager. Keep secret values out of prompts, logs, diffs, generated files, and copied `.env` content.
